title: Coordinates and graph of linear equations
competency: Draw the graphs of x = a, y = b and y = mx from a table of values.

keywords.def: A line parallel to the y-axis, like x = 4.
A line parallel to the x-axis, like y = 5.
A table of x values and the matching y values, used to draw a graph.
In y = mx, the number m.

ideas.name: Lines x = a and y = b

en.text: All points on the line x = a have x-coordinate a. It is a vertical line, parallel to the y-axis. All points on y = b have y-coordinate b. It is a horizontal line, parallel to the x-axis. x = −4 is 4 units left of the y-axis.

screens.title: What is the same?
screens.ask: The points (4, 4), (4, 2), (4, 0) and (4, −3) lie on one line. What do they share?
screens.after: Every point has x-coordinate 4. The line is x = 4, a vertical line.

screens.title: Graph of x = a
paras: Step 1: Make a table. For any y, the value of x stays a.
Step 3: Join them with a straight line.

screens.title: Note on x = a
paras: The graph of x = a is a line parallel to the y-axis.
If a is positive, the line is right of the y-axis. If a is negative, it is left.
If a = 0, the line is the y-axis itself.

screens.title: Graph of y = b
paras: For any x, the value of y stays b.
The graph of y = b is a line parallel to the x-axis.
If b is positive it is above the x-axis. If b is negative it is below. y = 0 is the x-axis.

points.info: On x = 4: the x-coordinate is always 4.
On y = 5: the y-coordinate is always 5.
On both lines: where x = 4 meets y = 5.

screens.title: Where is the line?
screens.ask: Tap each equation to see where its line is.
items: Vertical line, 4 units right of the y-axis.
Vertical line, 4 units left of the y-axis.
Horizontal line, 3 units above the x-axis.
Horizontal line, 2 units below the x-axis.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A line parallel to the y-axis, like x = 4.
A line parallel to the x-axis, like y = 5.
A table of x values and the matching y values, used to draw a graph.

screens.text: Graph of x = a: the graph of x = −4 is:
opts: A vertical line 4 units left of the y-axis
A vertical line 4 units right of the y-axis
A horizontal line 4 units below the x-axis
screens.ans: A vertical line 4 units left of the y-axis
screens.why:
x = a is a vertical line, parallel to the y-axis.
Here a = −4, which is negative.
Negative means left of the y-axis.
So it is a vertical line 4 units left.
A horizontal line would be y = −4.
screens.clue: x = a lines are parallel to the y-axis.

screens.text: Points on a line: tap every point that lies on the line y = 1.
screens.why:
A point is on y = 1 only if its y-coordinate is 1.
(−1, 1), (1, 1), (0, 1) and (−12, 1) have y = 1.
(0, 0), (1, 2) and (1, 15) have other y values.
The x-coordinate can be any number.
screens.clue: Look only at the second number.

screens.ask: Points on x = a: (m, 5), (m, 6) and (m, −2) lie on the line x = −8. m = ___
screens.why:
Every point on x = −8 has x-coordinate −8.
The first number of each point is m.
So m = −8.
screens.clue: What is x for every point on x = −8?

screens.text: Graph of x = a: the graph of x + 3 = 0 is:
screens.why:
Solve for x: subtract 3 from both sides.
x = −3.
x = a is a vertical line.
So it is the vertical line x = −3, 3 units left of the y-axis.

screens.ask: The lines x = −2 and y = 3 cross at one point. Tap it.
screens.why:
Every point on x = −2 has x = −2.
Every point on y = 3 has y = 3.
The crossing point must have both.
So it is (−2, 3).
screens.clue: Find the point whose x is −2 and whose y is 3.

screens.text: Horizontal or vertical? Which line contains both (2, −5) and (7, −5)?
screens.why:
Compare the points: x changes (2 and 7).
y stays the same: −5.
Points with the same y lie on a horizontal line.
The line is y = −5.
x = −5 is a vertical line, so it is wrong.
screens.clue: Which coordinate is the same in both points?

en.text: To graph y = mx, choose x values, find y = mx, plot the points and join them. The line always passes through the origin. If m > 0 it passes through Quadrants I and III. If m < 0 it passes through Quadrants II and IV. m is the slope.

screens.title: Find a point
screens.ask: y = 2x. If x = 3, what is y?
screens.after: y = 2 × 3 = 6. So (3, 6) is on the line.

screens.title: Graph of y = mx
paras: Step 1: Choose some values of x and find y.
Step 3: Join them with a straight line.

screens.title: Note
paras: y = mx passes through the 1st and 3rd quadrants when m > 0.
y = mx passes through the 2nd and 4th quadrants when m < 0.
For any m, the graph of y = mx passes through the origin.
In y = mx, m is called the slope of the line.

screens.title: Explore y = mx
screens.note: Try m = 2, then m = −2. With m > 0, x and y have the same sign (Quadrants I and III). With m < 0 the signs differ (II and IV). x = 0 always gives y = 0: the origin.

points.info: Both lines pass through the origin.

screens.title: Key words
defs: In y = mx, the number m.

screens.text: Graph of y = mx: which quadrants does y = −2x pass through?
screens.why:
In y = −2x, m = −2, which is negative.
When x > 0, y < 0: Quadrant IV.
When x < 0, y > 0: Quadrant II.
So the line passes through II and IV.

Put x = −3 into y = 4x.
y = 4 × (−3).
Positive times negative is negative.
y = −12.

screens.text: Sign of the slope: tap every line that passes through the 1st and 3rd quadrants.
screens.why:
Write each as y = mx.
y = 7x: m = 7. y − 12x = 0 is y = 12x: m = 12. y − x = 0 is y = x: m = 1.
y = −10x: m = −10. y + 6x = 0 is y = −6x: m = −6.
m > 0 means Quadrants I and III.
So tap y = 7x, y − 12x = 0 and y − x = 0.
screens.clue: Rewrite each as y = mx first.

screens.ask: Find the slope: the point (2, 8) lies on the line y = mx. m = ___
screens.why:
Put x = 2 and y = 8 into y = mx.
8 = m × 2.
Divide both sides by 2: m = 4.
Check: 4 × 2 = 8.
screens.clue: Put x = 2 and y = 8 into y = mx.

screens.ask: y = 3x. Tap the point on this line where x = −1.
screens.why:
Put x = −1 into y = 3x.
y = 3 × (−1) = −3.
The point is (−1, −3).
Go 1 left and 3 down.

screens.ask: Find the slope: 2y + 6x = 0 can be written as y = mx. The slope m = ___
screens.why:
Shift 6x to the right: 2y = −6x.
Divide both sides by 2: y = −3x.
Compare with y = mx: m = −3.
screens.clue: Get y alone on one side.

items.text: Graph of y = b: the graph of y = 5 is:
opts: A horizontal line 5 units above the x-axis
A vertical line 5 units right of the y-axis
items.ans: A horizontal line 5 units above the x-axis
items.why:
y = b is a horizontal line, parallel to the x-axis.
b = 5 is positive.
So the line is 5 units above the x-axis.
items.clue: y = b lines are parallel to the x-axis.

items.text: Graph of y = b: the graph of y = 0 is:
items.why:
Every point on y = 0 has y-coordinate 0.
Those points are all on the x-axis.
So y = 0 is the x-axis.
x = 0 is the y-axis, which is different.
items.clue: Read the Note on y = b.

items.text: Points on a line: which points lie on y = 1?
items.why:
Look at the second number of each point.
It must be 1.
(−1, 1), (1, 1), (0, 1), (−3, 1) and (−12, 1) have y = 1.
The others have y = 0, 2 or 15.

items.ask: Points on x = a: (m, 5), (m, 6) and (m, −2) lie on x = −8. m = ___
items.why:
Every point on x = −8 has x = −8.
m is the x-coordinate of each point.
So m = −8.
items.clue: What is x on that line?

items.text: Find the line: which line passes through (2, 3), (1, 3) and (−2, 3)?
items.why:
The x-coordinates change: 2, 1, −2.
The y-coordinate is always 3.
So the line is y = 3, a horizontal line.

items.text: Find the line: which line passes through (0, 0), (0, 1) and (0, −2)?
items.why:
The y-coordinates change: 0, 1, −2.
The x-coordinate is always 0.
So the line is x = 0, which is the y-axis.

items.text: Points on a line: which points lie on the line x = −2?
items.why:
Look at the first number of each point.
It must be −2.
(−2, 0), (−2, 1) and (−2, −3) have x = −2.
(0, −2) and (2, −2) have y = −2, not x = −2.

items.ask: Table of values for y = 4x: when x = 2, y = ___
items.why:
Put x = 2 into y = 4x.
y = 4 × 2 = 8.
The point (2, 8) is on the line.

items.ask: Table of values for y = 4x: when x = −1, y = ___
items.why:
Put x = −1 into y = 4x.
y = 4 × (−1) = −4.
The point (−1, −4) is on the line.

items.text: Sign of the slope: which lines pass through the 1st and 3rd quadrants?
items.why:
Rewrite each as y = mx.
y = 7x, y = 12x and y = x have m > 0.
y = −10x, y = −6x and y = −(3/2)x have m < 0.
m > 0 gives Quadrants I and III.

items.text: Sign of the slope: the line y + x = 0 passes through:
items.why:
Shift x: y = −x.
So m = −1, which is negative.
m < 0 gives Quadrants II and IV.
It passes through the origin too, but not only the origin.

items.ask: Find the slope: (2, 8) lies on y = mx. m = ___
items.why:
Substitute x = 2 and y = 8 into y = mx.
8 = 2m.
Divide by 2: m = 4.

test.text: Graph of x = a: the graph of x = 3 is:
test.why:
x = a is always a vertical line.
It is parallel to the y-axis.
x = 3 is 3 units right of the y-axis.

test.text: Sign of the slope: y = 5x passes through which quadrants?
test.why:
In y = 5x, m = 5, which is positive.
m > 0 gives Quadrants I and III.

test.text: Points on y = b: which point lies on the line y = −3?
test.why:
A point on y = −3 has y-coordinate −3.
(4, −3) has y = −3. Yes.
(−3, 4) has x = −3, not y = −3.
(−3, 0) has y = 0.

test.ask: Find the slope: the line y = mx passes through (−3, 12). m = ___
test.why:
Put x = −3 and y = 12 into y = mx.
12 = m × (−3).
Divide by −3: m = 12 ÷ (−3) = −4.
Check: −4 × (−3) = 12.

notes.text: No coordinate-plane block exists yet, so graphs are shown as tables of values and the students answer in words. A plotting block is needed (engine session).
Example 7 b prints the question "x + 3 = 0" but solves and graphs x − 3 = 0 (x = 3). The lesson uses x + 3 = 0 → x = −3. Teacher to confirm which is meant.
The headings print "of the form = a" and "= b"; they mean x = a and y = b. "Activity 2.3.3" should be Activity 3.3.3.
Coordinate-plane blocks (coord) added: tap-to-explore figures from the book examples and graded "plot the point" items.
Practice replays and tests now use fresh numbers from the int / sets / lineq / quad generators.
